key_insight: Ni sublattice order—not Ni concentration alone—governs local moments and magnetic ordering in intercalated NiₓNbS₂.
engineering_relevance: Controlling intercalant order may be essential for reproducible magnetism in layered materials, particularly disorder-prone thin films and heterostructures.
method: Measured Ni composition and ordering using energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy and synchrotron X-ray diffraction.
Mapped magnetic behavior with anisotropic susceptibility measurements.
Compared effective moments with DFT+U calculations for ordered Ni arrangements.
evidence_signal: Across single crystals with 0.10 ≤ x ≤ 0.57, long-range antiferromagnetism appeared only at 0.25 ≤ x ≤ 0.33, reaching Tₙ = 96 K at x = 1/3; dilute samples remained paramagnetic to 2 K, while Ni-rich samples showed short-range order below 10–15 K.
watch_item: Disorder-induced suppression of Ni-to-host charge transfer is an inferred mechanism; its applicability to thin films and heterostructures remains untested here.
paper_title: Interplay of Ni Order and Local Moments in Intercalated NixNbS2
